blocks.text: The module documentation distinguishes raising commit(), fail-open record_call(), preflight check(), and read-only usage_summary(). It also states that rows contain numeric measurements and opaque identifiers rather than prompt or output content.
blocks.title: Ledger responsibilities

blocks.text: Provider usage objects or mappings are inspected for cached prompt tokens. credits_for_call prefers a supplied dollar cost and otherwise converts token counts through the configured simple rate.
blocks.title: Usage extraction and placeholder pricing

blocks.text: commit validates surfaces and the system-account invariant, computes default credits, and inserts one usage_ledger row. record_call resolves ownership and catches every ledger failure so the hook never propagates it.
blocks.title: Writing usage rows

blocks.text: The read side sums credits by surface inside the plan period, rounds the values, and returns pool, used, remaining, reset, and user-surface fields for the usage API.
blocks.title: Period usage summary

blocks.text: CheckResult carries allowed status, pool values, reset time, and degraded state. check permits system calls, returns a degraded allow on database failure, and otherwise compares the estimate with remaining credits.

purpose: The ledger inserts one numeric usage row per call, attributes it to an account surface, and computes current-period totals from database rows. Recording and checking deliberately fail open so billing infrastructure cannot block a model call.
